seo.whatIsDesc: A modern, learn-while-playing Minesweeper. Classic 9×9 / 16×16 / 16×30 boards and flagging, plus a Learn Mode that computes the mine probability for every unopened cell in real time, overlays a 75% green-yellow-red heatmap, and scores each move 0-10 against the optimal choice. No right-click required — double-click to chord, perfect for trackpads and phones.
howToPlay: Left-click to open. First click never hits a mine; numbers show mines in the 8 neighbors.

Right-click to cycle marks: right-click cycles none → 🚩 → ❓ → none. 🚩 marks mines you're sure of, ❓ marks uncertain cells (costs no flag, can still be opened); the header shows mines remaining. Long-press works as right-click on mobile.

Double-click to chord (Apple / trackpad optimized): classic chording needs left+right together. Here, if flags around a number equal the number, double-click the number to open the rest — no right-click needed. Desktop left+right still works, and chording counts as a perfect 10.
Open all non-mine cells to win; hit a mine and the board reveals.
seo.heatmapDesc: With Learn Mode on, a solver builds constraints from opened numbers (exactly that many mines among the hidden neighbors; flags are only your own guesses and are ignored), splits frontier cells into components and enumerates, while isolated cells share the remaining mines evenly. Each cell gets P(mine) 0-1, shown as green (0%) → yellow (50%) → red (100%) at 75% opacity. Toggle % and fraction independently — color alone trains intuition.
seo.efficiencyTitle: Decision efficiency: how good was that move?
seo.efficiencyDesc: Fixed-gap scoring: it only measures how far your move was from the best option at that moment — score = 10 × (1 − |chosen prob − best prob| ÷ 0.5). Open is compared against the current lowest mine probability pMin, flag against pMax, unflag in reverse (the safer the cell you unflag, the higher the score). A 5-point gap costs only 1 point, so easy boards never punish you; a full 50-point gap drops to 0. Chording is always 10. Scores share the solver, so closing the heatmap still records for the post-game chart.
seo.chartTitle: How to read the replay chart
seo.chartDesc: It pops up at game over, with a time-window slider (drag both ends to zoom into any segment) and a JSON download. X is time, left Y is speed (areas), right Y is quality (lines) —
chartBullets: Open safe (teal area · left): RPM area chart, bucketed every 6s — the taller the area, the faster the flood-fill bursts.
Flag (red area · left): RPM area, also 6s buckets — when you were flagging.

Efficiency (orange dots+line · right 0-10): plotted at the exact click time. 10 = optimal at that moment; <6 red, <9 orange. Click any dot and the whole board restores to right after that move (opened cells, flags, question marks) for a true replay.
Mine prob (purple triangles, dashed · right 0-10 = prob×10): only for open/chord, the P(mine) of that cell at that moment. Overlay it with orange — high purple + low orange = a risky guess.
seo.chartHint: How to use it: find valleys in orange, check if purple spikes at the same time — that's the move to review. Click the dot and the board replays that moment; use the time slider to zoom into a busy segment; hit the download button to grab a JSON with every board snapshot for deep analysis.
progressSteps: Start with heatmap on, learn green=open, red=flag intuition;
Turn off %/fraction, decide by color alone, still aim for 10;
Turn Learn Mode off and challenge Hard 16×30 — keep RPM steady and orange ≥9.

items.a: Meathill Minesweeper (minesweeper.meathill.com) is a learn-while-playing Minesweeper with 9×9/16×16/16×30 boards, three-state right-click marks (flag/question), double-click chording, and Learn Mode: live probability heatmap + efficiency scoring, plus a post-game chart that replays the board to any moment (with snapshot download).

Constraints come only from opened numbers (each says: exactly N mines among my hidden neighbors — flags are ignored, since they may be wrong) on frontier cells, split into components and enumerated exactly, isolated cells share remaining mines evenly, yielding P(mine) 0-1 as green→yellow→red 75% overlay. Solver always runs for scoring.

Fixed-gap scoring, relative to the moment. Open is compared against the lowest mine probability pMin at that time, flag against pMax, unflag in reverse; score = 10 × (1 − gap ÷ 0.5). A 5-point gap costs 1 point; a 50-point gap costs all 10. Chord is always 10. Easy boards with near-equal options never get punished — only skipping clearly safer cells in dangerous spots costs real points. Each orange dot in the replay is one score — click it and the board replays that moment.

items.q: How to chord on Apple / trackpad?
items.a: Optimized: no left+right needed — double-click any opened number where flags == number to open the rest. Right-click, long-press, and trackpad all work, plus mobile.

items.q: How to read the replay chart?
items.a: Left Y = speed (areas), right Y = quality (lines). Teal/red RPM areas are 6s-bucketed for pace; orange dots are efficiency (0-10), purple triangles the cell's mine prob ×10 at that moment. When dots get dense, drag the time slider below the chart to zoom into a segment; click any operation dot and the whole board restores to right after that move; 'Back to final' restores the end position; the download button exports a JSON with every board snapshot.

Beginners use heatmap for intuition, intermediates use color only, experts turn Learn Mode off for Hard. Every game is reviewable.
